# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check |

# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

  ballisticVelocity(from, target, t, GRAVITY, vel);

}

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D browser game from the user prompt: "3d racket fight with super powers".

## Requirements
- Must be a 3D racket duel with superpowers, playable in a browser.
- Responsive desktop and mobile layout with touch controls.
- Auto-start capture compatibility: a visible button labeled exactly `PLAY` (or `Start`/`Play Game`/`Play Now`).
- No external runtime dependencies preferred; assets should be vendored.

## Decisions
- Game concept: **VOLT RALLY** — neon synthwave 3D tennis/racket duel vs AI “VEXA”, first to 7 points.
- Superpowers: Dash (`Q`), Time Warp (`E`, costs 35 charge), Super Smash (`R`, requires 100 charge, armed then consumed on next hit).
- Mechanics: move with WASD/mouse/touch joystick, swing with click/Space/SWING button, aim by cross-court positioning plus lateral input.
- Tech: static `index.html` + ES modules + vendored Three.js r184 + custom WebGL/canvas textures + procedural Web Audio; no build step.
- Visual approach: bloom, vignette/chromatic aberration postprocessing, reflective court, neon arena, synthwave skyline, holograms, crowd, particles, trails, shockwaves, camera shake.
- Scene split into `stage.js` (renderer/scene/ball/effects) and `game.js` (state/physics/AI/powers), with `ui.js` and `input.js`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Vendored Three.js r184 core and required addons into `vendor/three/`.
- Vendored Orbitron and Rajdhani WOFF2 fonts into `vendor/fonts/`.
- Created complete UI markup and styling in `index.html` / `styles.css`: menu, HUD, scoreboard, charge meter, power buttons, feed, banners, touch controls, result and pause overlays, loader.
- Implemented `src/utils.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/world.js`, `src/athlete.js`, `src/effects.js`, `src/stage.js`, `src/ui.js`, `src/input.js`.
- Implemented `src/game.js` core plus part 2: movement, AI, ball physics, net/floor collisions, scoring, powers, camera, markers, effects.
- Implemented `src/main.js` boot loop, loader hide, visibility pause, and `window.__VOLT_RALLY__` debug API.
- Syntax-checked all new JS files successfully with `node --check` via copied `.mjs` files.
- Fixed CSS touch overlay so it is hidden until `.on`; patched HUD charge/cooldown update logic.

### Active
- First browser run and visual/interaction debugging has not yet been done.
- Need to verify module imports, gameplay, scoring, AI, powers, mobile layout, and screenshots.
- Need to add/verify project README maybe, but not started.

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.

- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

## VOLT RALLY — Superpowered Racket Duel

A neon 3D racket duel against the arena champion, **VEXA**. Rally a plasma ball, bank perfect returns to charge your core, and unleash dash, time-warp and super-smash powers. First to **7 points** wins.

Built as a static, dependency-free browser game: Three.js and the display fonts are vendored, audio is synthesised with the Web Audio API, and there is no build step.

### Play

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3002
# then open http://localhost:3002
```

On an OMGithub workspace you can also run `./start.sh`, which uses the platform's static server.

### Controls

| Action | Desktop | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | `WASD` / arrow keys / mouse | Left virtual stick |
| Swing | Left click / `Space` | `SWING` button |
| Dash | `Q` | `DASH` |
| Time Warp | `E` (35% core) | `WARP` |
| Super Smash | `R` at 100% core | `SMASH` |
| Pause | `Esc` / `P` | Pause button |
| Mute | `M` / speaker button | Speaker button |

Move **across** the court as you swing to aim your return. Crossing the ball's path sends it to the opposite corner and pulls VEXA out of position. A perfectly timed swing in the centre of the racket charges the core faster — and a charged smash is unreturnable.

### Tech

- Three.js r184, vendored under `vendor/three/`
- Orbitron and Rajdhani, vendored under `vendor/fonts/`
- Custom shaders, post-processing (bloom + vignette), procedural textures and audio
- Responsive desktop, tablet, portrait and landscape touch layouts with safe-area support
- Debug surface at `window.__VOLT_RALLY__` for verification

### Credits

Three.js is © Three.js Authors, MIT licensed. Orbitron and Rajdhani are distributed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D browser game from the user prompt: "3d racket fight with super powers".

## Requirements
- Must be a 3D racket duel with superpowers, playable in a browser.
- Responsive desktop and mobile layout with touch controls.
- Auto-start capture compatibility: a visible button labeled exactly `PLAY` (or `Start`/`Play Game`/`Play Now`).
- No external runtime dependencies preferred; assets should be vendored.

## Decisions
- Game concept: **VOLT RALLY** — neon synthwave 3D tennis/racket duel vs AI “VEXA”, first to 7 points.
- Superpowers: Dash (`Q`), Time Warp (`E`, costs 35 charge), Super Smash (`R`, requires 100 charge, armed then consumed on next hit).
- Mechanics: move with WASD/mouse/touch joystick, swing with click/Space/SWING button, aim by cross-court positioning plus lateral input.
- Tech: static `index.html` + ES modules + vendored Three.js r184 + custom WebGL/canvas textures + procedural Web Audio; no build step.
- Visual approach: bloom, vignette/chromatic aberration postprocessing, reflective court, neon arena, synthwave skyline, holograms, crowd, particles, trails, shockwaves, camera shake.
- Scene split into `stage.js` (renderer/scene/ball/effects) and `game.js` (state/physics/AI/powers), with `ui.js` and `input.js`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Vendored Three.js r184 core/addons and Orbitron/Rajdhani WOFF2 fonts.
- Complete UI markup/styling in `index.html` / `styles.css`: menu, HUD, scoreboard, charge meter, powers, feed, banners, touch controls, result/pause overlays, loader.
- Implemented all game modules: `utils.js`, `audio.js`, `world.js`, `athlete.js`, `effects.js`, `stage.js`, `ui.js`, `input.js`, `game.js`, `main.js`.
- Fixed critical `ui.banner is not a function` bug by renaming the cached DOM node to `bannerEl` so the `banner()` method is no longer shadowed.
- Fixed out-of-bounds scoring order so a second bounce is `DOUBLE BOUNCE` for the hitter instead of incorrectly awarding `OUT` to the receiver.
- Added favicon data URI; removed favicon 404 and PCFSoftShadowMap deprecation warning.
- Tuned exposure/bloom/sun/ball lighting to remove severe washed-out overexposure.
- Reduced particle point-sprite scale (`320 → 18`) and point-burst size/count to prevent screen-filling glow blobs.
- Improved athlete visibility via lighter suit materials, emissive lift, and a per-athlete soft fill light.
- Fixed responsive menu layout: `flex-direction: column` under 820px, footer alignment, `touch-action: pan-y`, no horizontal page overflow.
- Added mobile charge meter above the HUD bottom deck; centered mobile scoreboard and hid desktop brand under 480px.
- Verified desktop, wide (1440×900), portrait (390×844, 320×568), and landscape (780×390) layouts.
- Verified auto-start via `#playBtn` (`PLAY`), gameplay, touch joystick movement, SWING button, power buttons, pause/resume/restart, victory result overlay, mute control, and Debug API.
- Added README game instructions and licensing files (`vendor/three/LICENSE`, `vendor/fonts/OFL-orbitron.txt`, `OFL-rajdhani.txt`).
- No JavaScript syntax errors; clean browser boot with only harmless SwiftShader ReadPixels warnings.
- All work is uncommitted; no git commit or push has been made.

### Active
- Final polish pass only; no known blocking runtime defects.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Optionally capture one final action screenshot after a hit/power to confirm particle tuning and HUD readability at 1050×790.
2. Verify a fresh browser session console has no errors after the latest CSS/athlete edits.
3. Review `README.md` formatting and ensure all new license files are present.
4. Commit/push if requested; currently all changes remain uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: app markup/import map/overlays/HUD/favicon.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: responsive neon UI, mobile charge meter, menu layout fixes.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: state/AI/physics/scoring/powers/camera; scoring and bloom tuning.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/stage.js`: renderer/scene/ball lighting/postprocessing bloom.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: court/stands/skyline/net/sun/arena.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/athlete.js`: player/VEXA meshes, rackets, suit materials, fill lights.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/effects.js`: particles/waves/trails/markers; point-size scale.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: HUD/overlay controller; banner naming fix.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/input.js`: keyboard/mouse/touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: procedural Web Audio SFX/music.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: boot loop, loader, debug API.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md`: game description, controls, run instructions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/vendor/three/`: vendored Three.js r184 + MIT license.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/vendor/fonts/`: vendored fonts + OFL license files.

## Important Context
- Runtime auto-detects static `index.html`; `start.sh` delegates to the platform static server. No `package.json` / build step.
- Capture auto-start matches exactly one visible button against `/^(?:start|play)(?:\s+(?:game|now))?$/i`; `PLAY` matches, `PLAY AGAIN` does not.
- Manual test server: `python3 -m http.server 3002`; browser opened at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright CLI expects Chromium 1243; symlinks were created from `chromium-1248` / `chromium_headless_shell-1248` to `-1243`.
- SwiftShader renders at ~4.5 FPS on 1050×790, so game time advances slowly during visual tests.
- HUD state fields consumed by `ui.update`: `playerScore`, `aiScore`, `charge`, `dashCd`, `warpCd`, `superArmed`, `rally`, `bestRally`, `phase`, `shots`, `elapsed`.
- Touch charge meter is positioned at `top: 118px` left and only shown under `body.touch`.
- The final tested build starts with 34% charge and auto-serves after a short delay.
- Screenshots are under `screenshots/` (gitignored).

20: ## VOLT RALLY — Superpowered Racket Duel
21: 
22: A neon 3D racket duel against the arena champion, **VEXA**. Rally a plasma ball, bank perfect returns to charge your core, and unleash dash, time-warp and super-smash powers. First to **7 points** wins.
23: 
24: Built as a static, dependency-free browser game: Three.js and the display fonts are vendored, audio is synthesised with the Web Audio API, and there is no build step.
25: 
26: ### Play
27: 
28: ```bash
29: python3 -m http.server 3002
30: # then open http://localhost:3002
31: ```
32: 
33: On an OMGithub workspace you can also run `./start.sh`, which uses the platform's static server.
34: 
35: ### Controls
36: 
37: | Action | Desktop | Touch |
38: | --- | --- | --- |
39: | Move | `WASD` / arrow keys / mouse | Left virtual stick |
40: | Swing | Left click / `Space` | `SWING` button |
41: | Dash | `Q` | `DASH` |
42: | Time Warp | `E` (35% core) | `WARP` |
43: | Super Smash | `R` at 100% core | `SMASH` |
44: | Pause | `Esc` / `P` | Pause button |
45: | Mute | `M` / speaker button | Speaker button |
46: 
47: Move **across** the court as you swing to aim your return. Crossing the ball's path sends it to the opposite corner and pulls VEXA out of position. A perfectly timed swing in the centre of the racket charges the core faster — and a charged smash is unreturnable.
48: 
49: ### Tech

51: - Three.js r184, vendored under `vendor/three/`
52: - Orbitron and Rajdhani, vendored under `vendor/fonts/`
53: - Custom shaders, post-processing (bloom + vignette), procedural textures and audio
54: - Responsive desktop, tablet, portrait and landscape touch layouts with safe-area support
55: - Debug surface at `window.__VOLT_RALLY__` for verification
